ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.claim: All authorities place the surah among the late Meccan revelations; Asad accepts the Itqan's placement immediately after surah 71, and its title comes from Abraham's prayer.
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.anchor: ALL AUTHORITIES agree that this surah belongs to the last group of Meccan revelations

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from Abraham’s episode and prayer, which asks security for Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, and prosperity for his progeny.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.anchor: the security of Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, prosperity for his progeny

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.claim: Abraham also prayed for forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.anchor: forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's prayers concern Makkah and his children settled there, showing Quraysh that their lives oppose his hopes while Muhammad and his followers fulfill them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The purpose is to make evident to the Quraysh that the whole life that they are leading is totally against the supplications and desires of Abraham (sws).

NAHHAS:v2p370/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p370/r6.claim: اجنبني has two objects; جنبني is an intensive form, while أجنبني is another available form.
NAHHAS:v2p370/r6.anchor: مفعولان ( واجنبني ) ويقال على التكثير جنبني ويقال أجنبني

NAHHAS:v2p370/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p370/r7.claim: أن نعبد is accusative and means “from worshipping idols.”
NAHHAS:v2p370/r7.anchor: في موضع نصب والمعنى من أن نعبد الأصنام

ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r3.claim: وأجنبني is read from أجنبتُه, ‘I put him at a distance’; جنبته has the same sense.
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r3.anchor:
وتقرأ (وأجنبني وبني) على أجنبتة كذا وكذا إذا جعلته ناحية منه، وكذلك
جنبته كذا وكذا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r4.claim: Abraham asks to remain protected from idol worship although he does not worship idols, just as ‘make us Muslims’ asks for continued firmness in Islam.
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r4.anchor:
ومعنى الدعاء من إبراهيم عليه السلام أن يجنب عبادة الأصنام، وهو
غير عابد لها على معنى ثبتني على اجتناب عبادتها كما قال:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r2.claim: “Keep me apart” means distance me and place me far away.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r2.anchor: بعدني واجعلني من على جانب بعيد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Quraysh's main defense of polytheism was that they inherited it from Abraham; the coming passage refutes that claim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The biggest argument cited by the Quraysh in favour of their polytheism was that they had inherited it from Abraham (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham settled his descendants in barren land after leaving a fertile region so they could establish a monotheistic worship center and avoid polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he had settled his progeny in a desolate and barren piece of land after he had migrated from a lush and green region.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r3.claim: Ibrahim asks that Mecca be safe; asking to make this town safe removes fear from an existing town, unlike making it one of the safe towns.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r3.anchor: بلدة مكة. { آمنا } ذا أمن لمن فيها، والفرق بينه وبين قوله: اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r4.claim: Ujnubnī means distance me and my sons from idols or put us apart from them; dialects differ, and the prayer shows prophets' protection depends on God, not all descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r4.anchor: بعدني وإياهم، { أن نعبد الأصنام } واجعلنا منها في جانب وقرىء { واجنبني } وهما على لغة نجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r5.speaker: ابن عيينة
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUyaynah argues Ishmael's descendants never worshipped idols; they circled stones called al-dawwār and treated a stone they set up as equivalent to the House.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:34-35/r5.anchor: وزعم ابن عيينة أن أولاد إسماعيل عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يعبدوا الصنم محتجا به وإنما كانت لهم حجارة يدورون بها

DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.claim: God answered Abraham’s prayer: none of his descendants worshiped idols after it, the town became safe and provisioned, and God made him a leader and guided his descendants to prayer, rites, and repentance.
DURR-FULL:v5p45/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وإذ قال ابراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.claim: Abraham’s attribution of guidance to God here, in 26:78, and in his prayer of 14:35 clearly establishes the author’s theological position.

SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r1.claim: In اجعل هذا البلد آمنا, البلد and آمنا are the two objects of causative جعل.
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { هذا البلد آمنا }: مفعولا الجعل التصييري

SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari contrasts this with 2:126: the earlier prayer asks that the town be one of the safe lands; here Ibrahim asks to transform a fearful town into a safe one.
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r2.anchor: قال الزممخشري: " فإن قلت: أي فرق بين قوله

SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r3.claim: Triliteral جنبه and quadriliteral أجنبه are Najdi forms; doubled جَنَّبه is Hijazi for preventing, from جانب. Al-Raghib derives it from distancing someone from a thing; another view likens it to leading a horse aside from shirk.
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r3.anchor: أجنبه إياه، ثلاثيا، ورباعيا، وهي لغة نجد، وجنبه إياه مشددا، وهي لغة الحجاز

SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r4.claim: The phrase أن نعبد omits a preposition: واجنبني عن أن نعبد.
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r4.anchor: و { أن نعبد } على حذف الحرف، أي: عن أن. وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى الثقفي

SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r5.speaker: الجحدري وعيسى الثقفي
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r5.claim: Al-Jahdari and ʿIsa al-Thaqafi read وأجنبني with hamzat qaṭʿ, from the quadriliteral form.
SAMIN-DURR:14:35/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى الثقفي " وأجنبني " بقطع الهمزة

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r1.claim: Abraham's prayer presents recognition of God's existence, oneness, and uniqueness, and rejection of belief in other powers, as the path to righteousness.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r1.anchor: recognition of God's existence, oneness and uniqueness and, hence, a rejection of all belief in

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r2.claim: The prayer expresses gratitude for God's bounty and links back to 14:34 and forward to 14:42.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n48/r2.anchor: it connects directly with the preceding verse 34 and the subsequent verse 42.

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n49/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n49/r1.claim: The land in Abraham's prayer is where the Kaaba stands, specifically Mecca.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n49/r1.anchor: I.e., the land in which the Kabah is situated

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r1.claim: Asnam, translated idols, is not limited to concrete images of false deities.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r1.anchor: asnam, sing. sanam) does not apply exclusively to actual, concrete representations of false

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r2.claim: Razi says shirk can include worshipful devotion to causal agencies and outward means such as wealth, power, luck, or people's favor.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r2.anchor: Razi points out, in a worshipful devotion to all manner of "causative agencies and outward means to an end"

ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r3.claim: True monotheism divests the heart of attachment to such agencies and recognizes no real directing power besides God.
ASAD-NOTES:14:35#n50/r3.anchor: genuine faith in the oneness and uniqueness of God (at-tawhid al-maha) consists in divesting oneself of all inner attachment to [such] causative agencies

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r9.claim: Abraham's first prayer predates Mecca becoming a known town, so it uses indefinite بلداً; the later prayer uses definite البلد for the established city.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r9.anchor: الآية الأولى هي دعاء سيدنا إبراهيم قبل أن تكون مكة بلداً فجاء بصيغة التنكير

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham made this prayer while settling Ishmael and his mother in Makkah, which then lacked security.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This supplication was made by Abraham (sws) when he was settling Ishmael (sws) and his mother in Makkah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God answered the prayer by making harm to animals, let alone people, a sin in Makkah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God accepted this request and even harming an animal in it was declared a sin, let alone human beings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Four months were made sacred so caravans could travel safely across Arabia; Quraysh's custody of the House gave them regional leadership and secure passage, with other tribes offering guides.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: In these months, caravans would be able to traverse peacefully from one part to another.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham asks protection from idolatry for himself and his descendants; including himself shows how great the danger of polytheism is, since many have succumbed to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The second thing he requested in this supplication was to protect him and his progeny from the filth of idol worship.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Although the word literally means sons, the dominant sense here is all Abraham's descendants, as confirmed by the following term for progeny.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: However, it is used keeping in view the dominant element.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi counts Rabbi or Rabbana seven times and says the apparent repetition is essential to supplication, which repeatedly humbles itself and seeks God's attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This apparently seems a repetition. Yet this is a feature of a supplication; in fact, it is essential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbi presents as grounds for the plea a favour of God the supplicant has personally experienced.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication the favour of God he has experienced.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbana presents as grounds for the plea a favour witnessed by all God's creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prayer is retold to Quraysh so they remember why they were settled in the barren valley, recognize Abraham's prayer as the source of their blessings, and see that they wrongly credit their alleged deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this supplication has been narrated to the Quraysh so that they recall the reason for being settled in this barren stretch of land

QIRAAT-ER:14:35:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:35:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:35:4#1/r1.claim: Ibrāhām has fatḥa on hāʾ and long ā before mīm, reflecting Aramaic or Syriac phonology closer to Abraham; it is canonical among the Seven.
QIRAAT-ER:14:35:4#1/r1.anchor: Variant vocalization with fatḥa on hāʾ and long ā before mīm — reflects Aramaic/Syriac phonology

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r1.claim: Jannaba has a light or doubled nūn in Hijazi usage, while ajnaba is Najdi; both mean to keep away, from the root sense of the side.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r1.anchor: جنب مخففا، وأجنب رباعيا لغة نجد، وجنب مشددا لغة الحجاز، والمعنى: منع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.claim: After condemning Quraysh and other Arabs for replacing God's favor with disbelief and idols, the passage recalls their ancestor Abraham: he prayed for Mecca's safety and his descendants' avoidance of idols, then settled them by the House for prayer, contrasting their father's faith with their idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.anchor: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه تعالى لما ذكر التعجيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that this passage calls the town definitely, while Abraham's prayer in al-Baqara uses an indefinite form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r19.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على قوله هنا هذا البلد معرفا، وفي البقرة منكرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the definite wording asks that this place be included among lands whose inhabitants are safe; the indefinite wording in al-Baqara asks to change a fearful town into a safe one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هنا سأل في الأول أن يجعله من جملة البلاد التي يأمن أهلها ولا يخافون، وفي الثاني أن يخرجه من صفة كان عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r2.claim: Abraham first asks for a safe place of worship, where worship can be performed without fear, then asks God to keep him and his sons continually away from idol worship; the sons are his immediate biological children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r2.anchor: ودعا إبراهيم أولا بما هو على طاعة الله تعالى، وهو كون محل العابد آمنا لا يخاف فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r3.claim: God answered by making the sanctuary safe; none of Abraham's immediate descendants worshipped an idol.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r3.anchor: وأجابه الله تعالى فجعل الحرم آمنا، ولم يعبد أحد من بنيه الأقرباء لصلبه صنما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r4.claim: Asked how Arabs came to worship idols, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said no descendant of Ishmael worshipped idols: they set up stones as symbolic Houses, circled them, and called the practice al-dawwār.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r4.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة: وقد سئل، كيف عبدت العرب الأصنام؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Abraham's prayer shows intense fear despite his rank, and the verse should model fear and seeking a good end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا الدعاء من الخليل عليه السلام يقتضي إفراط خوفه على نفسه، ومن حصل في رتبته فكيف يخاف أن يعبد صنما؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.claim: The repeated address to God is an appeal for compassion; Abraham explains his request by noting that he had seen his father and people worship idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r6.anchor: وكرر النداء استعطافا لربه تعالى، وذكر سبب طلبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r8.speaker: الجحدري وعيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r8.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read ajnibnī, from the verb ajnaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p444/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري، وعيسى الثقفي: وأجنبني من أجنب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r1.claim: Wa-idh is the object of an omitted verb, “remember,” recalling the event in the style of similar passages.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r1.anchor: مفعول لفعل محذوف أي أذكر ذلك الوقت والمقصود تذكير

ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r3.claim: Āminan means a place possessing security, like denominative adjectives labin and tāmir, since the residents are truly safe; it may also figuratively attribute a state to its location, as in “a flowing river.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r3.anchor: أي ذا أمن فصيغة فاعل للنسب كلابن وتامر لأن الآمن في الحقيقة أهل البلد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf distinguishes this prayer from 2:126: here Abraham asks for the town to be among places whose inhabitants are safe, whereas there he asks to change a fearful place into a secure one.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r4.anchor: والفرق بين ما هنا وما في البقرة من قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s distinction follows the second object’s role as the point of information: “make this a good ring” asks for a kind of object, while “make this ring good” asks only for its quality.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r5.anchor: كذا في الكشاف وتحقيقه أنك إذا قلت : اجعل هذا خاتما حسنا فقد أشرت إلى المادة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r6.claim: On that account, the first prayer asks for both townhood and security, while the second asks for security alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r6.anchor: في الأول سؤال أمرين البلدية والأمن وههنا سؤال أمر واحد وهو الأمن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that this distinction entails that the request for townhood preceded the prayer in this sūra, and that the first prayer went unanswered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p232/r7.anchor: واستشكل هذا التفسير بأنه يقتضي أن يكون سؤال البلدية سابقا على السؤال المحكي في هذه السورة وأنه يلزم أن تكون الدعوة الأولى غير مستجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r1.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r1.claim: Kashf reconciles the requests by taking the first as asking that the land become continuously habitable and safe for its residents, since it had not been fit for settlement.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r1.anchor: أما بأن المسؤول أولا صلوحه للسكنى بأن يؤمن فيه أهله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r2.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r2.claim: Kashf also offers alternatives: safety may be protection from occasional danger, a request for lasting security stated hyperbolically, worldly versus afterlife safety, or a second prayer before the first was answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r2.anchor: وأما بالحمل على الاستدامة وتنزيله منزلة العاري عنه مبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r3.claim: Kashf reads the wording as progression: Abraham first asks that this become a safe town, then stresses the request because it is actually fearful; a distressed person's prayer is nearer to being answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r3.anchor: وكأنه بنى الكلام على الترقي فطلب أولا أن يكون بلدا آمنا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r4.claim: Some take the passage as one request retold, while others infer two requests from the changed wording; al-Ālūsī's apparent conclusion is that both townhood and safety were requested.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers that the townhood request is retold in 14:37 as hearts inclining to Abraham's family for residence, as Ibn ʿAbbās explains, not merely pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.anchor: إذ المسؤول هويها إليهم المساكنة كما روى عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r6.claim: Another explanation is that security is especially relevant to gratitude, making it apt to mention while rebuking the unbelievers for neglecting God's favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r6.anchor: لأن نعمة الا من أدخل في استيجاب الشكر فذكره انسب بمقام تقريع

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative is an aside reinforcing the preceding call to gratitude through faith and good works and warning against their opposites; it gently invites the Meccan rejecters.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.anchor: واردة على سبيل الاعتراض مقررة لما حث عليه من الشكر بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.claim: Irshād says the passage heightens the Prophet's astonishment: Quraysh denied special and general blessings, disobeyed Abraham, and replaced the sacred city with ruin despite God's answered prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.anchor: وفي إرشاد العقل السليم أن المراد منها تأكيد ماسلف من تعجيبه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r1.speaker: الجحدري وعيسى الثقفي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r1.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read the verb with hamza qatʿ and a kasra on the nūn, on the pattern of أكرمني.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى الثقفي ( وأجنبني ) بقطع الهمزة وكسر النون

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r2.claim: The alternate form reflects Najdi usage, which has both the light form جنبه and the quadriliteral أجنبَه; the Ḥijāzī form doubles the middle consonant.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r2.anchor: جنبه مخففا وأجنبه رباعيا وأما أهل الحجاز فيقولون

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r3.claim: The root image of tajannub is being on a different side from another person, then by extension being distant.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r3.anchor: وأصل التجنب أن يكون الرجل في جانب غير ما عليه غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the prayer as asking God to keep Abraham and his children steadfast in monotheism, Islam, and avoidance of idols, since prophets are protected from unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r4.anchor: والمراد هنا على ماقال الزجاج طلب الثبات والدوام على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that Abraham asked out of humility and to display his need for God's grace in every matter, although he knew God protected him from idolatry.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r5.anchor: الأول أنه عليه السلام وإن كان يعلم أن الله تعالى يعصمه من عبادة الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r6.speaker: الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r6.claim: The Sufis distinguish manifest shirk from hidden shirk, attachment of the heart to apparent means; Abraham may be asking for freedom from this subtler attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r6.anchor: والثاني أن الصوفية يقولون : الشرك نوعان ظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that the Sufi account raises the same question: if looking to anything besides God resembles shirk, prophets are already protected from it, so why ask?
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r7.anchor: ويرد على هذا الأخير أنه يعود السؤال عليه فيما أظن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī's preferred answer is that prophetic protection is not an innate trait but comes solely through God's enabling grace, so seeking it is meaningful.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r8.anchor: والجواب الصحيح عندي ماقيل : إن عصمة الأنبياء عليهم السلام ليست لأمر طبيعي فيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r9.speaker: الله سبحانه
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r9.claim: A report says God told Moses not to feel secure from divine plan until he had crossed the bridge; al-Ālūsī offers this as a possible source of the need to seek protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234/r9.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن الله سبحانه قال لموسى عليه السلام : ياموسى لاتأمن مكري حتى تجوز الصراط

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r1.claim: Even people promised Paradise by the truthful Prophet often asked God for it; al-Ālūsī suggests the warning to Moses may explain this practice of seeking what is assured.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r1.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن المبشرين بالجنة على لسان الصادق المصدوق عليه الصلاة والسلام كانوا كثيرا مايسألون الله تعالى الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r2.claim: The apparent meaning of Abraham's sons is his direct offspring; Quraysh's idolatry does not require concluding that his prayer went unanswered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r2.anchor: والمتبادر من بنيه عليه السلام من كان من صلبه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r3.claim: Some restrict the intended sons to those already alive when Abraham prayed, thereby avoiding the apparent problem posed by later idolatrous descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r3.anchor: بما قاله بعضهم من أن المراد كل من كان موجودا حال الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī also allows that the prayer was answered for some descendants but not others, which would not imply any deficiency in Abraham's supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r4.anchor: أو بأن دعاءه استجيب في بعض دون بعض ولا نقص فيه كما قال الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r5.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna says Abraham's sons includes all his descendants and claims no Ishmaelite worshipped an image-idol; each people instead set up a stone and circumambulated it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r5.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة : إن المراد ببنيه مايشمل جميع ذريته عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r6.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna says people called their installed stone al-dawwār; this is why some disliked saying one circumambulates around the House and preferred the verb ṭāfa bihi.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r6.anchor: وكانوا يدورون به ويسمونه الدوار ولهذا كره غير واحد أن يقال دار بالبيت

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid similarly says no descendant of Abraham worshipped an image-idol, though some worshipped an unfigured object; he distinguishes ṣanam from wathan by whether it is fashioned as an image.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r7.anchor: لم يعبد أحد من ولد إبراهيم عليه السلام صنما وانما عبد بعضهم الوثن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that the Qur'an repeatedly condemns Quraysh for idol worship, which these explanations appear to overlook.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r8.anchor: وليت شعري كيف ذهبت على هذين الجليلين مافي القرآن من قوارع تنعى على قريش عبادة الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī calls Mujāhid's distinction weak: Abraham meant worship of anything besides God, and an idol-image and an unfigured idol are equivalent in that respect; the same objection applies to Ibn ʿUyayna.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r9.anchor: قال الإمام بعد نقله كلام مجاهد : إن هذا ليس بقوى لأنه عليه السلام لم يرد بهذا الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r10.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r10.claim: Some of al-Ālūsī's school infer that only God distances people from unbelief and brings them near to faith, since Abraham asks God for that distance; al-Ālūsī says the inference is problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p234#2/r10.anchor: واستدل بعض أصحابنا بالآية على أن التبعيد من الكفر والتقريب من الإيمان ليس إلا من الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.claim: The 'city' in Abraham's prayer is the Sacred Precinct.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد} يعني: الحرم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r2.claim: Āminan means secure, a place where people are safe.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r3.claim: Ajنبnī means keep me far away.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r4.claim: The forms janabtuhu, ajnabtuhu, jannabtuhu, and ijtanabtuhu express the same sense.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r4.anchor: يقال: جنبته الشيء، وأجنبته جنبا، وجنبته تجنيبا واجتنبته اجتنابا بمعنى واحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.claim: An objection asks how Abraham, protected from idolatry, could pray for protection, and how the prayer was answered when many descendants worshipped idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r5.anchor: فإن قيل: قد كان إبراهيم عليه السلام معصوما من عبادة الأصنام، فكيف يستقيم السؤال؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r6.claim: One answer is that Abraham prayed for an increase in protection and steadfastness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r6.anchor: قيل: الدعاء في حق إبراهيم عليه السلام لزيادة العصمة والتثبيت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r7.claim: One answer takes his sons to mean his own immediate offspring, none of whom worshipped idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r7.anchor: وأما دعاؤه لبنيه: فأراد بنيه من صلبه، ولم يعبد منهم أحد الصنم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r8.claim: Another answer says Abraham's prayer concerned only whichever of his descendants were believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p354#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن دعاءه لمن كان مؤمنا من بنيه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r1.claim: After establishing that God created and owns all things, the passage recalls Abraham to expose the descendants' ingratitude, idolatry by imitation of forefathers, and neglect of prayer and gratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r1.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم أن يذكروهم بأيام الله عند أبيهم إبراهيم عليه السلام للدلالة على تبديلهم النعمة ظلما منهم وكفرا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r2.claim: The reminder of God's past favors through Abraham also signals resurrection and the need to disavow idols, even though Abraham was their greatest forefather.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r2.anchor: مشير إلى وجوب براءتهم من الأصنام حيث كان محط حالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r3.claim: The opening means, 'Remember for them' the account of God's dealings with Abraham.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r3.anchor: أي واذكر لهم مذكرا بأيام الله خبر إبراهيم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r4.claim: The definite 'this city' is Mecca, the place from which the opponents want to expel the Messenger and whose people threaten those granted its blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r4.anchor: أي الذي يريدون إخراج الرسول منه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r5.claim: Abraham's prayer in this passage came after people had settled in Mecca; his earlier prayer in al-Baqara was made in an empty valley, asking first that it become a town and then that it be secure.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r5.anchor: وكأن هذا الدعاء صدر منه بعد أن سكن الناس مكة وصارت مدينة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r6.claim: Safety means that the inhabitants' lives and property are secure and the soul is at rest from danger.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r6.anchor: وهو سكون النفس إلى زوال الضر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r7.claim: After asking for bodily and property security, Abraham asks for religious security: turn him and his sons aside from idol worship and place them on another side.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r8.claim: The sons are Abraham's own male descendants; the mention omits daughters as an indication of male independence, since daughters are dependent.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r9.claim: The prayer asks for lasting separation from worship of idols, an act that would merit the Fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p189/r9.anchor: أي عبادة مستمرة تكون موجبة للنار

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r1.claim: The Prophet calls himself the answer to Abraham’s prayer and says the banner of praise will be in his hand on Judgment Day, with Arabs nearest to it.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r1.anchor: وهي دعوة أبينا إبراهيم ولواء الحمد بيدي يوم القيامة ومن أقرب الناس إلى لوائي يومئذ العرب

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r2.speaker: عقيل بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r2.claim: At Aqaba, six Ansar asked to hear revelation; the Prophet recited Abraham’s prayer through the end of the sura, and they accepted.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r2.anchor: عن عقيل بن أبي طالب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أتاه الستة نفر من الأنصار جلس إليهم عند جمرة العقبة

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi asks who can feel safe from trial after Abraham prayed to be kept from idolatry.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي قال: من يأمن البلاء بعد قول إبراهيم {واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام}

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r4.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna says no descendant of Ishmael worshipped idols because Abraham’s prayer was specific to this town and its people.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r4.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة قال: لم يعبد أحد من ولد إسماعيل الأصنام لقوله: {واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r1.claim: The verse connects to 14:28: Meccans failed to thank God for blessings granted through answering Abraham’s prayer, abandoned their righteous forebears’ example for misguided ancestors, and repaid Abraham’s prayer with ingratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمة الله كفرا ( إبراهيم : 28 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r2.claim: Alternatively, it coordinates with the account of God creating the heavens and earth: the discourse moves from general blessings, which include Mecca, to blessings specific to its people, praising Abraham and alluding to his polytheist descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون معطوفة على جملة الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض } بأن انتقل من ذكر النعم العامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r3.claim: Idh is an accusative time noun governed by an omitted common verb, estimated as ‘remember when’; it heightens wonder at the polytheists as in 14:28 and recalls the same lesson.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r3.anchor: اسم زمان ماض منصوب على المفعولية لفعل محذوف شائع الحذف في أمثاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r4.claim: Rabb is a vocative with the calling particle omitted; its original form is rabbī, with the first-person yāʾ commonly dropped for lightness in vocatives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r4.anchor: و { رب } منادى محذوف منه حرف النداء . وأصله ( ربي )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r5.claim: Al-balad means a specified tract of land and can also mean a town; the definite article marks a known place, and al-balad apposes the demonstrative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r5.anchor: والبلد : المكان المعين من الأرض ، ويطلق على القرية . والتعريف في { البلد } تعريف العهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.claim: The prayer leaves the town unnamed, either to create suspense before identifying it as the place near the Sacred House, or because Arabs knew it meant Mecca. This matches 2:126: here Abraham asks this city to be safe; there he asks that the indicated place become one of the safe cities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.anchor: وحكاية دعائه بدون بيان البلد إبهام يرد بعده البيان بقوله : { عند بيتك المحرم ( سورة إبراهيم : 37 )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r1.claim: The phrase means “remember when Abraham said.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r2.claim: The land Abraham refers to is Mecca.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r2.anchor: المعنى: واذكر إذ قال إبراهيم، والبلد: مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r3.claim: Āminan means that security exists there; describing the place as secure is figurative, as in the “stormy day” and a poet's “sleepless camel-night.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r3.anchor: وآمنا معناه فيه أمن، فوصفه بالأمن تجوزا- كما قال: في يوم عاصف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r4.claim: Ajnibnī means protect or prevent me; janabahu, jannabahu, and ajnabahu all mean to keep someone from something.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r4.anchor: واجنبني معناه: وامنعني، يقال: جنبه كذا وجنبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r5.speaker: الجحدري والثقفي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r5.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and al-Thaqafī read ajnibnī with a hamza and kasra on the nūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري والثقفي «وأجنبني» بقطع الألف وكسر النون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r6.claim: Abraham means his own sons; his prayer was answered among them, while other descendants worshipped idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r6.anchor: وأراد إبراهيم بني صلبه، وكذلك أجيبت دعوته فيهم، وأما باقي نسله فعبدوا الأصنام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r7.claim: Abraham's fear of idolatry despite his rank should be emulated through reverent fear and prayer for a good end.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r7.anchor: لكن هذه الآية ينبغي أن يقتدى بها في الخوف وطلب الخاتمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r8.speaker: الطبري عن مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī, citing Mujāhid, defines aṣnām as sculptures shaped like humans; objects carved in other forms are awthān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r8.anchor: والأصنام هي المنحوتة على خلقة البشر، وما كان منحوتا على غير خلقة البشر فهي أوثان، قاله الطبري عن مجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet recited these verses, prayed for his community, and received good news about them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r14.anchor: وأسند الطبري عن عبد الله بن عمر حديثا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: تلا هاتين الآيتين ثم دعا لأمته،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r15.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r15.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Taymī asks who can feel safe after Abraham, God's close friend, feared idolatry for himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r15.anchor: وكان إبراهيم التيمي يقول: من يأمن على نفسه بعد خوف إبراهيم الخليل على نفسه من عبادة الأصنام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r16.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r16.claim: The poet's phrase “the camel's night is not sleeping” supports figurative attribution of a state to a place or time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p340#2/r16.anchor: وكما قال الشاعر: وما ليل المطي بنائم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r1.claim: The request that this town be secure was explained earlier under al-Baqara 126.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ اجعل هذا البلد آمنا ﴾ قد سبق تفسيره في سورة ( البقرة 126 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r2.claim: ‘Keep me and my sons away’ means keep us apart from idol worship and make us steadfast in avoiding it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p365#2/r2.anchor: أي جنبني وإياهم والمعنى ثبتني على اجتناب عبادتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr presents Abraham's prayer as evidence against Arab polytheists: Mecca's sanctuary was founded for worship of God alone, and Abraham rejected worship of anyone else.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r1.anchor: مكة إنما وضعت أول ما وضعت على عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، وأن إبراهيم الذي كانت عامرة بسببه، آهلة تبرأ ممن عبد غير الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r2.claim: God answered Abraham's prayer for Mecca's safety, as confirmed by 29:67 and 3:96–97.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r2.anchor: وقد استجاب الله له، فقال تعالى: {أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr infers this prayer came after the House was built; Abraham's earlier prayer when he left infant Ishmael and Hagar at Mecca said “make this a town,” and Ishmael preceded Isaac by thirteen years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r3.anchor: فعرفه كأنه دعا به بعد بنائها؛ ولهذا قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r4.claim: Every person making supplication should pray for themselves, their parents, and their descendants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p512#2/r4.anchor: ينبغي لكل داع أن يدعو لنفسه ولوالديه ولذريته

JISHUMI:v5p3879/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r4.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r4.claim: Some read اجنبني with hamza, others without; al-Zajjaj says the hamzated form means putting someone aside and is equivalent to جنبته.
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r4.anchor: قرأ بعضهم: (أجنبني) بالهمز، وبعضهم بغير همز، قال الزجاج

JISHUMI:v5p3879/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r5.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r5.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿIsa glosses أجنبني as 'turn me away from it.'
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r5.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: أجنبني: اصرفني عنه

JISHUMI:v5p3879/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r6.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Hijaz speakers use the light form as in the Quran, while speakers of Najd use either form.
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: أهل الحجاز يقولون: جنبني شره بالتخفيف وبذلك نزل القرآن

JISHUMI:v5p3879/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r7.claim: An idol is a sculpted image; an object without an image is a wathan.
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r7.anchor: والصنم: التمثال المصور، وما ليس بصنم فهو وثن

JISHUMI:v5p3879/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r8.claim: The verb governing إذ is omitted and understood as 'remember when he said.'
JISHUMI:v5p3879/r8.anchor: العامل في قوله: (إذ) محذوف، تقديره: واذكر إذ قال

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r1.claim: Abu al-Qasim says it is permissible to pray devotionally for what one knows will happen: Abraham knew God would keep him from idolatry and unbelief.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r1.anchor: قال أبو القاسم: وتدل على جواز الدعاء بما يعلم قطعا أنه كائن تعبدا وتذللا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r1.claim: “This town” is the Sacred City; God increased its safety, protected it from aggressors, and answered Abraham's prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r1.anchor: هاذا البلد } يعني البلد الحرام ، زاده الله أمنا ، وكفاه كل باغ وظالم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r2.claim: In 2:126 Abraham first asks that it be made a town whose inhabitants are safe; here he asks that an already fearful town be changed into a safe one.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r2.anchor: قد سأل في الأول أن يجعله من جملة البلاد التي يأمن أهلها ولا يخافون ، وفي الثاني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r3.anchor: { واجنبني } وقرىء : ( وأجنبني ) ، وفيه ثلاث لغات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r4.claim: The verb has three forms: the Hijazis use the doubled form, while Najdis use janabnī or ajnibnī; the prayer asks God to keep them continually from idol worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r4.anchor: فأهل الحجاز يقولون : جنبني شره بالتشديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r5.claim: “My sons” means Abraham's biological sons and their descendants.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r6.speaker: ابن عيينة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r6.claim: Asked how Arabs worshipped idols, Ibn ʿUyayna said no descendant of Ishmael worshipped an idol, citing Abraham's prayer; he said tribes erected stones as substitutes for the House, circled them, and called this practice al-dawwār.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r6.anchor: وسئل ابن عيينة : كيف عبدت العرب الأصنام ؟ فقال : ما عبد أحد من ولد إسماعيل صنما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r7.claim: These were stones each tribe treated as a substitute for the House and circled; he prefers saying “circumambulated the House” rather than “circled the House.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p523#2/r7.anchor: قالوا : البيت حجر ، فحيثما نصبنا حجرا فهو بمنزلة البيت ، فكانوا يدورون بذلك الحجر

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r1.claim: The city is Mecca, which was a place of safety for its people in the pre-Islamic period.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r1.anchor: يعني مكة، فكان أمنا لهم في الجاهلية

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r2.claim: Bani means Ibrahim's children; he knew his descendants would differ in their affirmation of God's oneness.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r2.anchor: وقد علم أن ذريته مختلفون في التوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r1.claim: The opening means: remember when Abraham said this prayer.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r2.claim: This is the sacred city. Unlike 2:126, Abraham now asks that a city already characterized by fear be turned into a safe one, rather than merely included among safe cities.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r2.anchor: الفرق بين هذه وبين ما في البقرة أنه قد سأل فيها أن يجعل من جملة البلدان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r3.claim: Ajunibnī means distance me from idol worship and keep me continually avoiding it, as in the prayer to make us Muslims to You.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r3.anchor: وبعدنى أي ثبتنى وأدمنى على اجتناب عبادتها كما قال واجعلنا مسلمين لك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232/r4.claim: By his sons Abraham meant his biological sons.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r1.claim: The “town” Abraham asks God to make secure is Mecca; its explanation was given earlier in al-Baqarah.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r2.claim: Ijnubni means put me apart from worshipping idols.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r3.claim: Abraham means his biological sons; he had eight, and none of them worshipped an idol.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r3.anchor: وأراد بقوله: «بني» بنيه من صلبه وكانوا ثمانية، فما عبد أحد منهم صنما

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r4.claim: Another view takes the prayer to be for whichever descendants God intends to guide.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو دعاء لمن أراد الله أن يدعو له

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r5.speaker: الجحدري وعيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r5.claim: Al-Jahdari and ʿIsa read wa-ajنبnī with a hamza cut, while the meaning remains the same.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى «وأجنبني» بقطع الألف والمعنى واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r6.claim: The forms janabtu, ajnabtu, and jannabtu all convey avoiding or leaving something, including the imperative ajtanibhu.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r6.anchor: يقال: جنبت ذلك الأمر وأجنبته وجنبته إياه فتجانبه واجتنبه أي تركه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r7.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r7.claim: In a sermon, Ibrahim al-Taymi warns that no one can feel safe from trial after Abraham prayed to be kept from idols, as his father and people had worshipped them.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:35-36/r7.anchor: وكان إبراهيم التيمي يقول في قصصه: من يأمن البلاء بعد الخليل حين يقول { واجنبنى وبنى أن نعبد الأصنام }

QASHANI:14:35-38/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r1.claim: Abraham represents the spirit speaking through its state as it turns to God seeking direct witnessing.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r1.anchor: الروح بلسان الحال عند التوجه إلى الله في طلب الشهود

QASHANI:14:35-38/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r2.claim: The city is the bodily realm; its safety is freedom from the dominance of soul-qualities, conflict among faculties, and tug of desires.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r2.anchor: من غلبات صفات النفس وتنازع القوى وتجاذب الأهواء

QASHANI:14:35-38/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r3.claim: His sons are the theoretical and practical intellects, thought, intuition, remembrance, and other faculties; he asks that they not love and worship idols of multiplicity arising from sense, bodily desire, and nature.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r3.anchor: وغيرها. { أن نعبد } أصنام الكثرة عن المشتهيات الحسية

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r1.claim: After the preceding proofs that only God may be worshipped, the passage recounts Abraham's emphatic rejection of idol worship.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r1.anchor: لما بين بالدلائل المتقدمة أنه لا معبود إلا الله سبحانه وأنه لا يجوز عبادة غيره تعالى ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r2.claim: Abraham asks that Mecca be made secure. “Make this a town secure” asks that it join the secure towns; “make this town secure” removes its existing fear and gives it the opposite quality.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r2.anchor: سأل في الأول أن يجعله من جملة البلاد التي يأمن أهلها فلا يخافون

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r3.claim: The reading واجنبني has three related Arabic forms. Al-Farrāʾ says the Hijaz uses the lightened جنبني يجبني, while Najd uses جنبني شره or وأجنبني شره.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r3.anchor: قرىء { واجنبني } وفيه ثلاث لغات جنبه واجنبه وجنبه

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r4.claim: The root sense is to put one thing away from another, to a side or apart.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r4.anchor: وأصله جعل الشيء عن غيره على جانب وناحية

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r5.claim: An objection says Abraham asked for Mecca's safety, yet God did not grant it because people later destroyed the Kaaba and raided Mecca.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r5.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام دعا ربه أن يجعل مكة آمنا ، وما قبل الله دعاءه

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r6.claim: An objection asks why a prophet who never worships an idol would pray to be kept from doing so.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r6.anchor: أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يعبدون الوثن ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r7.claim: A further objection says Abraham's prayer that his sons avoid idols was unanswered because Quraysh, among his descendants, worshipped idols; restricting “sons” to direct sons returns to the prophet objection.
RAZI-FULL:v19p103#2/r7.anchor: أنه طلب من الله تعالى أن لا يجعل أبناءه من عبدة الأصنام والله تعالى لم يقبل دعاءه

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r1.claim: One answer says Abraham prayed after building the Kaaba that the city be protected from destruction.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r1.anchor: أنه نقل أنه عليه السلام لما فرغ من بناء الكعبة ذكر هذا الدعاء ، والمراد منه : جعل تلك البلدة آمنة من الخراب

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r2.claim: Most exegetes take “the town” to mean its inhabitants, as “ask the town” in Qur'an 12:82 means ask its people.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r2.anchor: أن المراد جعل أهلها آمنين ، كقوله : { واسئل القرية } ( يوسف : 82 )

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r3.claim: On the inhabitants reading, Mecca has a special security: refugees are safe there, enemies meet without fear, and wild animals approach people there unlike elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r3.anchor: ما اختصت به مكة من حصول مزيد من الأمن ، وهو أن الخائف كان إذا التجأ إلى مكة أمن

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r4.claim: Another answer takes the request as a command and judgment that the town be secure, which was certainly fulfilled.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r4.anchor: وذلك الأمر والحكم حاصل لا محالة .

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r5.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the request as “keep me firm in avoiding idol worship,” like the prayer “make us Muslims for You” in Qur'an 2:128.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه ثبتني على اجتناب عبادتها كما قال : { واجعلنا مسلمين لك }

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r6.claim: Razi says the question remains: if God certainly keeps prophets from idol worship, the request still needs an explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r6.anchor: السؤال باق لأنه لأنه لما كان من المعلوم أنه تعالى يثبت الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r7.claim: Abraham may have prayed despite knowing God would protect him, as an act of humility and an acknowledgment of constant need for divine grace.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r7.anchor: أنه عليه السلام وإن كان يعلم أنه تعالى يعصمه من عبادة الأصنام إلا أنه ذكر ذلك هضما للنفس وإظهارا للحاجة والفاقة إلى فضل الله

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r8.speaker: الصوفية
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r8.claim: Sufis distinguish manifest shirk, professed by idolaters, from hidden shirk: attachment of the heart to intermediaries and apparent causes; pure monotheism sees no agent besides God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r8.anchor: شرك جلي وهو الذي يقول به المشركون ، وشرك خفي وهو تعليق القلب بالوسايط

RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r9.claim: Razi suggests Abraham's prayer may seek protection from this hidden shirk of relying on intermediaries.
RAZI-FULL:v19p104/r9.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون قوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام } المراد منه أن يعصمه

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r1.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf says “my sons” means Abraham's direct sons; the prayer's benefit is the same as in his request for himself.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قوله ( وبني ) أراد بنيه من صلبه

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r2.claim: Some say Abraham meant all descendants then alive, both children and grandchildren; his prayer was certainly answered for them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم أراد من أولاده وأولاد أولاده كل من كانوا موجودين حال الدعاء ولا شبهة أن دعوته مجابة فيهم

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r3.claim: Mujāhid says none of Abraham's descendants worshipped an image-idol; an aṣnām is an image, while an unfigured object is a wathan, and Quraysh worshipped stones and trees.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد : لم يعبد أحد من ولد إبراهيم عليه السلام صنما ، والصنم هو التمثال

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r4.claim: Razi rejects Mujāhid's distinction as weak: Abraham's prayer must concern worship of anything besides God, and stones are equivalent to idols for that purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r4.anchor: وهذا الجواب ليس بقوي ، لأنه عليه السلام لا يجوز أن يريد بهذا الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r6.claim: Alternatively, God answered Abraham's general prayer for some descendants but not all; this does not diminish prophets, as God's covenant excluded wrongdoers in Qur'an 2:124.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r6.anchor: لعله وإن كان عمم في الدعاء إلا أن الله تعالى أجاب دعاءه في حق البعض دون البعض

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r7.claim: Razi's Ashʿarite proof infers that God alone turns people away from disbelief and toward faith, since Abraham asks God to keep him and his children from it.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r7.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بقوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام } على أن الكفر والإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r8.claim: The Muʿtazilite interpretation that this asks for لطف is rejected as departing from the apparent meaning and from objections already given against that explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v19p105/r8.anchor: وقول المعتزلة إنه محمول على الألطاف فاسد ، لأنه عدول عن الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r3.claim: The second request is for monotheism and protection from associating partners with God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r3.anchor: والمطلوب الثاني : أن يرزقه الله التوحيد ، ويصونه عن الشرك ، وهو قوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام }

RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r1.claim: Al-Razi's associates argue that Abraham's plea to avoid idol worship shows that God alone grants abstention from prohibited acts.
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r1.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بهذا الآية على أن أفعال العبد مخلوقة لله تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r1.claim: As Abraham asks for Mecca’s security, inwardly he asks that his heart be a safe abode containing nothing but God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r1.anchor: كما سأل أن يجعل مكة بلدا آمنا طلب أن يجعل قلبه محلا آمنا

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r2.claim: An idol is anything worshipped apart from God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r2.anchor: والصنم ما يعبد من دونه ، قال تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r3.claim: The verse about taking one’s desire as a god (45:23) illustrates that an idol need not be a physical statue.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r3.anchor: والصنم ما يعبد من دونه ، قال تعالى : { أفرءيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه }

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r4.claim: Each person’s idol is whatever distracts from God, including wealth, children, status, obedience, or worship.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r4.anchor: فصنم كل أحد ما يشغله عن الله تعالى من مال وولد وجاه

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r5.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r5.claim: When building the House, Abraham asked God to free him from noticing his own self and deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r5.anchor: ويقال إنه لما بنى البيت استعان بالله أن يجرده من ملاحظة نفسه وفعله

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r6.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r6.claim: One account says Abraham moved between witnessing God’s favor and his own poverty: divine generosity prompted his prayer for his father, while self-poverty prompted his plea for protection from idols.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r6.anchor: فلما لقي من فضله وجوده قال قال من كمال بسطه

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r7.claim: Another account says Abraham prayed for his father when witnessing God’s favor, mercy, and gentleness, and prayed against idolatry when he saw others’ condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r7.anchor: ويقال شاهد غيره فقال : { واجنبنى وبنى أن نعبد الأصنام }

STUDYQURAN:14:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r1.claim: One account says that after Hagar bore Ishmael, jealous Sarah prompted Abraham to take Hagar and Ishmael from Syria to Mecca; therefore the land is Mecca.
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r1.anchor: It is said that when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael, Sarah became jealous of her; so Abraham took Hagar and Ishmael from Syria to Makkah.

STUDYQURAN:14:35/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r2.claim: Some identify 29:67 as the answer to Abraham's prayer that Mecca be made secure.
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r2.anchor: Some commentators see the answer to Abraham’s prayer that Makkah be made secure in the wording of 29:67

STUDYQURAN:14:35/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r3.claim: Abraham asks that he and his children be kept entirely distant from idol worship.
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r3.anchor: When Abraham says, Keep me and my children from worshipping idols, he is saying, “Make me and my children totally distant from idol worship” (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:14:35/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r4.claim: Another aspect of Abraham's prayer at Mecca is discussed in the commentary on 2:126–129.
STUDYQURAN:14:35/r4.anchor: For another aspect of Abraham’s prayer at Makkah, see commentary on 2:126–29.

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r1.claim: In the preceding prayer, Abraham asks that the sanctuary be safe and its inhabitants secure.

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r2.claim: Tabari lists several Arabic verb forms for keeping someone apart from evil: janabtu, jannabtu, and ajnabtu.
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r2.anchor: وتنفض مهده شفقا عليه … وتجنبه قلائصنا الصعابا

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r3.claim: Abraham asks to be distanced, along with his sons, from worshipping idols; a line using jannabtu illustrates the verb.
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى ذلك: أبعدني وبني من عبادة الأصنام،

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r4.claim: Aṣnām is the plural of ṣanam, an image or statue; Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj uses ṣanam for a woman's image in a verse.
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r4.anchor: والأصنام: جمع صنم، والصنم: هو التمثال المصور، كما قال رؤبة بن العجاج في صفة امرأة: [البحر الرجز] وهنانة كالزون يجلى صنمه

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says God answered Abraham's prayer so that none of his descendants worshipped a ṣanam afterward; he distinguishes a ṣanam as an image from other idols called awthān.
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا، واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام} [إبراهيم: 35] قال: " فاستجاب الله لإبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid lists other answers to Abraham's supplication: God secured the town, provided its people with fruit, made Abraham a leader, and gave him descendants who establish prayer and rites.
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r6.anchor: قال: واستجاب الله له، وجعل هذا البلد آمنا، ورزق أهله من الثمرات، وجعله إماما،

TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r7.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r7.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Taymī warns that no one is secure from trial, since even God's close friend prayed that he and his sons be kept from idol worship.
TAB-FULL:v13p686#2/r7.anchor: عن مغيرة، قال: كان إبراهيم التيمي يقص، ويقول في قصصه: " من يأمن من البلاء بعد خليل الله إبراهيم،

SULAMI:v1p347/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p347/r1.claim: Ibrahim's request that the town be safe asks that his own heart be secured from separation and veiling.
SULAMI:v1p347/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أراد بهذا أن يجعل

SULAMI:v1p347/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r2.speaker: السياري
SULAMI:v1p347/r2.claim: The idols from which Ibrahim asks protection are the passions one follows.

SULAMI:v1p347/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r3.speaker: الدينوري
SULAMI:v1p347/r3.claim: People's idols take many forms: the self, children, wealth, trade, spouse, or one's spiritual state; each person is bound to one.
SULAMI:v1p347/r3.anchor: قال الدينوري : الأصنام مختلفة فمنهم من صنمه نفسه ، ومنهم من صنمه ولده

SULAMI:v1p347/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r4.speaker: الدينوري
SULAMI:v1p347/r4.claim: Disavowing these idols means claiming no spiritual state or impossibility for oneself, relying on no deed, and returning blame for every good or evil to oneself without self-satisfaction.
SULAMI:v1p347/r4.anchor: كل واحد من الخلق مربوط بصنم من هذه الأصنام ، والتبرىء أي من هذه الأصنام

SULAMI:v1p347/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r5.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p347/r5.claim: Ja'far reads the prayer as asking not to be returned to witnessing Abraham's intimate friendship with God, nor his children to witnessing prophethood.
SULAMI:v1p347/r5.anchor: قال جعفر : لا تردني إلى مشاهدة الخلة ولا ترد أولادي

SULAMI:v1p347/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p347/r6.claim: After God ordered Abraham to build the Kaaba, He rebuked him for asking acceptance as though the building were his favor; Abraham had forgotten God's benefaction and foregrounded his own deed.
SULAMI:v1p347/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إن الله تعالى أمر إبراهيم ببناء الكعبة

SULAMI:v1p347/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p347/r7.claim: The self is the worst idol when it follows desire and its own interests; Abraham asks that God occupy the self and cut it off from all besides Him.
SULAMI:v1p347/r7.anchor: قال : واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام أي نفسي شر صنم

SULAMI:v1p347/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p347/r8.claim: The idols of intimacy and reliance are intrusive thoughts of heedlessness and fleeting moments of attachment.
SULAMI:v1p347/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أن تعبد أصنام الخلة والركون إليها وهو خطرات

SULAMI:v1p347/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p347/r9.claim: Every self has an idol of desire, except the self purified through divine enabling.
SULAMI:v1p347/r9.anchor: وقال أيضا : أن تعبد الأنفس لأن لكل نفس صنما من الهوى

SULAMI:v1p347/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p347/r10.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p347/r10.claim: Junayd reads the prayer as asking to be prevented from drawing near to God through anything besides God.
SULAMI:v1p347/r10.anchor: قال الجنيد : واجنبني وبني ، أي امنعني

TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r2.claim: Abraham’s prayer to keep his descendants from idolatry and misguidance asks for their protection from sin, which al-Tabataba’i identifies with infallibility; broadly understood descendants include deviants, so ‘sons’ means the Prophet and his purified, infallible progeny.
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r2.anchor: وهي العصمة، ومن المعلوم أن ذرية إبراهيم وإسماعيل - وهم عرب مضر أو قريش خاصة - فيهم ضال ومشرك

TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r5.claim: Although Abraham names idolatry, he explains it as misguidance; the author therefore takes the prayer to cover every kind of deviation and shirk, including sins.
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r5.anchor: إلا أنه عليه السلام علله بالضلال فأنتج سؤال التطهير من جميع الضلال من عبادة الأصنام ومن أي شرك حتى المعاصي

TABATABAI:14:35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35/r1.claim: These verses give a second reminder of blessings, following the reminder of Moses and Israel in 14:6: now they recount blessings for descendants of Abraham through Ishmael, including guidance away from idols, Meccan security, affection, and provision.
TABATABAI:14:35/r1.anchor: تتضمن الآيات تذكرة ثانية بجملة من نعمه عقيب التذكرة الأولى

TABATABAI:14:35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35/r2.anchor: والإشارة إلى مكة شرفها الله تعالى

TABATABAI:14:35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35/r3.claim: Comparing this prayer with Abraham's prayer in 2:126 suggests two occasions: first he asked for a town and provisions after settling Ishmael and Hagar; later, finding a town established, he asked that it be secure.
TABATABAI:14:35/r3.anchor: اختلاف المحكيين في التعبير أعني قوله { اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا } وقوله { اجعل هذا البلد آمنا } أنهما دعاءان

TABATABAI:14:35/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35/r4.claim: The distinction is supported by the earlier prayer asking provision for the town's inhabitants, while this passage asks it specifically for Abraham's descendants and adds other requests; this would be Abraham's last prayer quoted in the Qur'an, after Jurhum joined the family and Mecca was built.
TABATABAI:14:35/r4.anchor: في آية البقرة الدعاء لأهل البلد بالرزق من الثمرات وفي الآيات المبحوث عنها الدعاء بذلك لذريته خاصة مع أمور أخرى دعا بها لهم

TABATABAI:14:35/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35/r5.claim: If both accounts are one prayer, the wording can be reconstructed as “make this town a secure town,” with either “town” or its descriptive noun omitted for brevity in one account.
TABATABAI:14:35/r5.anchor: وعلى تقدير أن يكون المحكيان دعاء واحدا يكون قوله { رب اجعل } الخ تقديره رب اجعل هذا البلد بلدا آمنا

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r1.claim: The requested security is legislative, not physical: Abraham asks God to establish the law of sanctity and safety for Mecca.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r1.anchor: والمراد بالأمن الذي سأله عليه السلام الأمن التشريعي دون التكويني - كما تقدم في تفسير آية البقرة -

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r2.claim: Mecca's sacred status has generated immense religious and worldly blessings for its residents and the righteous attached to it; history records much, but more remains unrecorded, making its security a great divine favor.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r2.anchor: وجدنا ما لا يحصى من الخيرات والبركات الدينية والدنيوية عائدة إلى أهلها وإلى سائر أهل الحق ممن يحن إليهم

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r3.claim: The verbs janaba and ajnaba mean to keep away or distance; Abraham asks God to distance him and his sons from idol worship as refuge from the idols' misguidance.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r3.anchor: يقال جنبه وأجنبه أي أبعده، وسؤاله عليه السلام أن يجنبه الله ويبعده وبنيه من عبادة الأصنام

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r4.claim: Divine protection does not compel or strip people of choice; coercive protection would have no merit and would not be what Abraham, God's intimate friend, asks for.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r4.anchor: غير أنه ليس بنحو يؤدي إلى الإلجاء والاضطرار ولا ينجر إلى القهر والإجبار بسلب صفة الاختيار منه

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r5.claim: Good acts and abstentions are first attributed to God and second to the servant; evil is attributed first to the servant, and to God only as requital.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r5.anchor: أن كل خير من فعل أو ترك فإنه منسوب إليه تعالى أولا، ثم إلى العبد ثانيا بخلاف الشر من فعل أو ترك فإنه منسوب إلى العبد ابتداء

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r6.claim: Avoiding idolatry and receiving guidance are divine gifts that the servant owns only through God's grant; reports of the Imams summarize this as God enabling a servant to do good and leave evil.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r6.anchor: أبسط كلمة في هذا المعنى ما وقع في أخبار آل العصمة أن الله يوفق عبده لفعل الخير وترك الشر

TABATABAI:14:35-36/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r7.claim: Abraham asks for God's protection and guidance when he and his sons make themselves receptive, not a protection imposed regardless of their choices or receptivity.
TABATABAI:14:35-36/r7.anchor: أن يحفظه وبنيه من عبادة الأصنام ويهديهم إلى الحق إن هم عرضوا أنفسهم لذلك وأن يفيض عليهم إن استفاضوا

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r1.claim: Although the prayer's wording includes all those addressed, its effect reaches those prepared to receive it, not the stubborn and arrogant.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r1.anchor: أن نتيجة الدعاء لبعض المدعوين لهم وإن كان بلفظ يستوعب الجميع، وهذا البعض هم المستعدون لذلك دون المعاندين والمستكبرين منهم

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r2.claim: “My sons” can include all later descendants through both Ishmael and Isaac, since son can mean a remote descendant; the Qur'an's “your father Abraham's community” and repeated “children of Israel” illustrate this usage.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r2.anchor: وبنوه جميع من جاء من نسله بعده وهم بنو إسماعيل وبنو إسحاق فإن الابن كما يطلق على الولد من غير واسطة كذلك يطلق على غيره

TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r3.speaker: author
