TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r3.claim: A possible contextual restriction is that Abraham meant only the descendants of Ishmael living in the Hijaz, not the descendants of Isaac.
TABATABAI:14:35-36#2/r3.anchor: اللهم إلا أن يقال إن قرائن الحال والمقال تدل على اختصاص الدعاة بآل إسماعيل القاطنين بالحجاز فلا يعم بني إسحاق

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r1.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r1.claim: Commentators object that the prayer seems unanswered because Quraysh, among Abraham’s descendants, worshipped idols.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r1.anchor: استشكلوا أولا قوله عليه السلام { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام } من حيث إن ظاهره سؤال الحفظ

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r2.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r2.claim: They also ask why the Qur’an would quote an unfulfilled prayer as purposeless speech without stating its rejection, unlike its usual practice.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r2.anchor: وهو لغو غير معنى به ثم لا يذكر رده

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r3.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r3.claim: A further objection is that an infallible prophet should not ask to be protected from idol worship.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r3.anchor: ثم كيف يمكن أن يسأل لنفسه المصونية والعصمة عن عبادة الأصنام وهو نبي والأنبياء معصومون

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r4.claim: One answer takes “my sons” as immediate sons such as Ishmael and Isaac, for whom the prayer was answered.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r4.anchor: قيل في الجواب عن إشكال عدم استجابة دعائه في بنيه أن المراد ببنيه أبناؤه بلا واسطة

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r5.claim: Another answer restricts “my sons” to descendants alive when Abraham prayed, who were monotheists.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد الموجودون من بنيه وقت الدعاء وهم موحدون

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r6.claim: A third answer says God answered the prayer for some descendants but not all, without any deficiency in that outcome.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r6.anchor: وقيل إن الله قد استجاب دعاءه في بعض بنيه دون بعض ولا نقص فيه

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r7.claim: Some say Abraham’s polytheist descendants treated idols as intercessors rather than worshipping them.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r7.anchor: وقيل إن المشركين من بنيه لم يكونوا يعبدون الأصنام وإنما كانوا يتخذونها شفعاء

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r8.claim: Another distinction says they worshipped unfigured idols (awthān), not figured statues (aṣnām).
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r8.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يعبدون الأوثان دون الأصنام وبينهما فرق فإن الأصنام هي التماثيل المصورة

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r9.claim: A further account says each person set up a stone, called it like the Kaaba, circled it, and named this practice al-dawwār.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r9.anchor: وقيل إنهم ما كانوا يعبدون الأصنام بل كان الواحد منهم ينصب حجرا ويقول هذا حجر والبيت حجر

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r10.claim: He rejects the first two answers as contrary to the wording, the partial-answer explanation as missing the real objection, and the remaining distinctions because all involve worshipful association.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r10.anchor: وسقوط هذه الوجوه ظاهرة أما الأول والثاني فلكونهما خلاف ظاهر اللفظ وأما الثالث فلأن الإشكال ليس في ورود نقص

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r11.claim: One answer reads the request as asking for continued, lasting protection from idolatry.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r11.anchor: وقيل في الجواب عن إشكال سؤال النبي الإبعاد والإجناب عن الشرك وهو نبي معصوم أن المراد الثبات والدوام على ذلك

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r12.claim: Another answer sees Abraham as humbling himself and displaying his dependence on divine grace.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r12.anchor: وقيل إنه عليه السلام ذكر ذلك هضما لنفسه وإظهارا للحاجة إلى فضله تعالى

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r13.claim: A third answer takes the request as protection from hidden association, since prophets are protected from manifest association.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r13.anchor: وقيل المراد سؤال الحفظ عن الشرك الخفي وإلا فالأنبياء مصونون عن الشرك الجلى

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r14.claim: He rejects the permanence answer: if infallibility is necessary from the start, it remains necessary, so asking for its continuance is no less problematic.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r14.anchor: أما الأول فلأنه لا ينحسم به مادة الإشكال إذ العصمة والمصونية كما أنها لازمة للنبوة حدوثا لازمة لها بقاء

TABATABAI:14:35-41/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r15.claim: Divine bestowal does not make its recipient independent: need persists, God’s ownership and power remain, and asking expresses need rather than prior deprivation.
TABATABAI:14:35-41/r15.anchor: فإن الحاجة من جانب المستفيض باقية على حالها قبل الإفاضة لا تختلف أصلا

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r1.claim: Self-abasement applies to nonessential matters, not necessary infallibility; denying essential human status would merely deny perfection, and the proposed display of need also fails on their premise.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r1.anchor: هضم النفس إنما يستقيم في غير الضروريات وأما الأمور الضرورية فلا

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r2.claim: He rejects the hidden-association answer: Abraham explains the request by saying idols led many astray, so he asks protection from manifest idolatry, not inward reliance on other than God.
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r2.anchor: فهو إنما يسأل الإبعاد من عبادة هذه الأصنام وهي الشرك الجلي دون الحفظ عن الركون والتوجه إلى غير الله

TABATABAI:14:36#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:36#3/r3.claim: Equating idols with everything one turns toward besides God, and worship with any such orientation, is an unsupported reinterpretation.

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.claim: The repeated vocatives vary between “my Lord” and “our Lord”: requests specific to Abraham’s precedence and imamate use the singular, while shared requests use the plural.
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.anchor: النداء المكرر الذي فيه بلفظ { رب } و { ربنا } والعناية فيما أضيف

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r2.speaker: عقيل بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r2.claim: A report in al-Durr al-Manthūr says the Prophet recited Abraham’s prayer from this sura to six men of the Ansar at al-ʿAqaba; they were moved and responded to his invitation.
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r2.anchor: عن عقيل بن أبي طالب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لما أتاه الستة النفر

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r5.claim: He calls apparently reported claims that Ishmael’s descendants never worshipped idols after Abraham’s prayer, but merely treated them as intercessors, likely fabricated, in light of his preceding argument.
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r5.anchor: أن الرواية موضوعة، وقد تقدمت الإشارة إليه

TABRISI:14:37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r1.speaker: الجحدري والثقفي وأبو الجحجاح
TABRISI:14:37/r1.claim: These readers pronounce the hamza of واجنبني as hamzat al-qaṭʿ.
TABRISI:14:37/r1.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة الجحدري والثقفي وأبي الجحجاح واجنبني بقطع الهمزة

TABRISI:14:37/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37/r9.claim: Arabic uses janabtu and ajnabtu for avoiding something; here Ibrahim asks God to turn him and his sons away from idol worship.
TABRISI:14:37/r9.anchor: يقال جنبت الشيء أجنبه جنوبا ومن العرب من يقول أجنبته أجنبه

TABRISI:14:37#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r6.claim: The address tells Muhammad to recall Ibrahim's prayer for Mecca and its sanctuary; a report places it after he completed the Kaʿba.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r6.anchor: يعني مكة وما حولها من الحرم وقيل إن إبراهيم ع لما فرغ من بناء الكعبة دعا بهذا الدعاء

TABRISI:14:37#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r7.claim: The earlier indefinite baladan becomes definite when repeated as hādhā al-balad; the same repetition appears in 24:35.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r7.anchor: لأن النكرة إذا تكررت وأعيدت صارت معرفة

TABRISI:14:37#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r8.claim: God answered Ibrahim's prayer: people seeing their father's killer in the sanctuary would not attack, and wild animals approached them safely.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r8.anchor: فاستجاب الله دعاء إبراهيم ع حتى كان الإنسان يرى قاتل أبيه فيها فلا يتعرض له

TABRISI:14:37#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r9.claim: Ibrahim asks for divine لطف that enables him and his sons to avoid idol worship.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r9.anchor: أي والطف لي ولبني لطفا نتجنب به عن عبادة الأصنام

TABRISI:14:37#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r10.claim: Prophets' prayers are answered; Ibrahim's request concerns descendants God knew would believe, and God permitted and answered it.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r10.anchor: ودعاء الأنبياء لا يكون إلا مستجابا فعلى هذا يكون سؤاله ذلك مخصوصا بمن علم الله

TABRISI:14:39-41/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:39-41/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:39-41/r11.claim: The passage follows the ban on idol worship and command to worship God by showing Ibrahim's rejection of idols and prayer; alternatives connect it to Moses' mission or God's granting requests.
TABRISI:14:39-41/r11.anchor: اتصلت الآيات بما قبلها لأن النهي عن عبادة الأصنام والأمر بعبادة الله سبحانه قد تقدم

FARRA:v2p78/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p78/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p78/r3.claim: Hijazis say جَنِّبني lightly; Najdis say أَجْنِبني or جَنِّبني. وأجنبني is valid, though al-Farrāʾ had not heard a reader use it.
FARRA:v2p78/r3.anchor:
أهل الحجاز يقولون: جنبني ، هي خفيفة.
وأهل نجد يقولون: أجنبني شره وجنبني شره.

THALABI:v5p321/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p321/r1.claim: The verb for keeping someone away occurs in several forms; Umayya ibn al-Ashkar's verse attests tajannabahu.
THALABI:v5p321/r1.anchor: ويقال جنبته أجنبه جنبا وأجنبته إجنابا بمعنى وأجنبك وجنبته تجنيبا

THALABI:v5p321/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r2.speaker: أمية بن الأشكر الليثي
THALABI:v5p321/r2.claim: Umayya ibn al-Ashkar al-Laythi's line uses tajannabahu for keeping someone away.
THALABI:v5p321/r2.anchor: وتنفض مهده شفقا عليه … وتجنبه فلا يصعي الصعابا

THALABI:v5p321/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p321/r3.claim: Aṣnām is the plural of ṣanam, a carved image or statue; a poem is cited as evidence.
THALABI:v5p321/r3.anchor: والأصنام جمع صنم وهو التمثال المصور

THALABI:v5p321/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321/r4.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
THALABI:v5p321/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi asks who can feel secure from trial after Abraham prayed that he and his sons be kept from idol worship.
THALABI:v5p321/r4.anchor: وقال إبراهيم التيمي في قصصه: من يأمن من البلاء بعد خليل الله إبراهيم (عليه السلام)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p233#3/r1.claim: The plea means “keep me and them away,” with “them” understood for the children.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi refers the explanation of Ibrahim's request for a secure town to his earlier discussion in Surat al-Baqara.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r1.anchor: تفسير هذا قد سبق في سورة البقرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r2.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i similarly notes the Hijaz and Najd forms for asking someone to be kept apart.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ajnabtu or jannabtu something means putting it aside or at a distance; Abu Ubayda cites a poem by Umayya ibn al-Askar using jannabahu.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أجنبته كذا وكذا: جعلته ناحية منه وجانبا، وكذلك جنبته وجنبته (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda cites Umayya ibn al-Askar's line about keeping a child apart as evidence for the sense of jannabahu.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r4.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة لأمية بن الأسكر: وتنفض مهده شفقا عليه ... وتجنبه قلائصنا الصعابا (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says Ibrahim already avoided idols, so he asks God to keep him steadfast in that avoidance, like the prayer make us submit to You.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ومعنى الدعاء من إبراهيم أن يجنب عبادة الأصنام، وهو غير عابد لها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r6.claim: Some scholars of meaning restrict his prayer for his children to those God permitted him to pray for, since prophetic prayers are answered, although some descendants worshiped idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r6.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل المعاني قوله: {وبني} دعاء لمن أذن الله في أن يدعو له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r7.claim: Another view takes bani as his sons directly from his own loins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r7.anchor: أو خص بهذه الدعوة أبناءه من صلبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r8.claim: A sanam is an image that is worshiped; its plural is asnam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p483/r8.anchor: والصنم: الصورة التي تعبد، وجمعه أصنام (¬4)

MAJAZ:v1p342/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p342/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p342/r1.claim: Ajunubnī means keep me and my sons away; janabtu and janabttuhu are equivalent forms, illustrated by an anonymous line and Dhu al-Rumma’s intensified ajnibuhu.
MAJAZ:v1p342/r1.anchor: واجنبني وبني» (35) : جنبت الرجل الأمر، وهو يجنب أخاه الشر وجنبته واحد، وقال:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r1.claim: The city Abraham asks God to make secure is Mecca; after recalling blessings to humanity in 14:28–34, the passage recalls the special blessings given the Meccans through the answer to Abraham's prayer and calls for gratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r1.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim’in, güvenli kılmasını Allah’tan istediği şehir Mekke’dir. Allah Teâlâ önceki âyetlerde (28-34) genel olarak insanlığa verdiği nimetleri hatırlatmıştı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.claim: The account presents Abraham's grateful devotion and supplication as an example of servitude to God, and points to salvation through his monotheistic way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.anchor: Ayrıca Allah’ın verdiği sayısız ve sınırsız nimetlerin şükrünü yerine getiren bir kulun yani Hz. İbrâhim’in Allah’a karşı tutumu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r3.claim: Asnam means anything besides God credited with divine power or attributes and revered in worship as a means of shirk.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r3.anchor: esnâm (tekili sanem) kelimesi, Allah’tan başka kendisine ilâhî güç veya nitelikler yakıştırılarak tapınma duygusu içerisinde değer verilen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r4.claim: “Idols” can refer to the people who make idols and invent and practice idol worship; idolatry has led many people astray.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r4.anchor: “Putlar”dan maksat, onları yapanlar, puta tapmayı icat edip uygulayanlardır. Bu mânada putlar (putperestlik) birçok insanın sapmasına yol açmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r5.claim: Abraham first asks for the city's safety because religious and worldly duties cannot be fulfilled where life and property are insecure, then asks protection from idolatry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r5.anchor: Can ve mal güvenliğinin bulunmadığı bir yerde dinî ve dünyevî görevler yerine getirilemeyeceği için Hz. İbrâhim öncelikle beldenin güvenli kılınmasını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.claim: Commentators say Abraham made the prayer in these verses after Mecca had become a settlement and he and Ishmael had built the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.anchor: Müfessirlere göre İbrâhim bu âyetlerde bildirilen duasını da Mekke yerleşim merkezi haline geldikten ve İsmâil ile birlikte Kâbe’yi inşa ettikten sonra yapmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.claim: God answered Abraham's prayer by making Mecca secure and bringing produce grown elsewhere for worship such as pilgrimage and for trade; the commentary also directs readers to passages on Mecca and the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.anchor: Allah Hz. İbrâhim’in duasını kabul ederek Mekke’yi güvenli bir şehir haline getirmiş ve dünyanın muhtelif yerlerinde yetiştirilen ürünlerin gerek hac ve umre gibi ibadetler

BURHAN:v1p126/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p126/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p126/r4.claim: Al-Baqara has baladan as the second object and āminan its adjective; Ibrahim has al-balad as first object and āminan as second, pointing back to the barren valley.
BURHAN:v1p126/r4.anchor: ﴿ بلدا ﴾ هنا هو المفعول الثانى و ﴿ آمنا ﴾ صفته

ITQAN:v3p306/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p306/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p306/r7.claim: Ibrahim first prayed to make the valley a town before Hajar and Ishmael settled there; later, after it became a town inhabited by Jurhum, he prayed for its security, explaining indefinite versus definite wording.
ITQAN:v3p306/r7.anchor: لأن الأول دعا به قبل مصيره بلدا عند ترك هاجر وإسماعيل به وهو واد

BURHAN:v2p64/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p64/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p64/r3.claim: One explanation distinguishes Abraham's first prayer at a place, asking it to become a secure town, from the later prayer for security in a town; another asks for security to endure.
BURHAN:v2p64/r3.anchor: لأنه في الدعوة الأولى كان مكانا فطلب منه أن يجعله بلدا آمنا

BURHAN:v2p64/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p64/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p64/r4.claim: The author answers the apparent chronological objection: the Qur'an's order of reporting need not match Abraham's order, and some Meccan revelation came after the Hijra, even after the conquest.
BURHAN:v2p64/r4.anchor: وكون سورة البقرة مدنية وسورة إبراهيم مكية لا ينافي هذا
